title: Graded comparison for convolution tensor of filtered K-flat complexes
statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative ring and let $P,Q$ be integer cochain complexes of $R$-modules [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], with finite decreasing filtrations by subcomplexes [def-sp-filtration]. Assume that each module $P^n,(F^iP)^n,(\operatorname{gr}^iP)^n,Q^n,(F^jQ)^n,(\operatorname{gr}^jQ)^n$ is flat (its tensor functor preserves exact sequences), and that each complex $P,F^iP,\operatorname{gr}^iP,Q,F^jQ,\operatorname{gr}^jQ$ is K-flat [def-pc-module-kflat-complex]; graded complexes mean successive quotients [def-sp-filtered-complex-subquotients]. On the total tensor complex $T=\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes_R Q)$ [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves], specialized to ordinary modules by using the one-point site with ring $R$, define the convolution filtration by
$$G^aT=\sum_{i+j=a}\operatorname{im}\bigl(\operatorname{Tot}(F^iP\otimes_R F^jQ)\longrightarrow T\bigr).$$
This is a finite filtration, its underlying, step and graded modules are flat, and its underlying, step and graded complexes are K-flat. There are canonical isomorphisms of cochain complexes
$$\bigoplus_{i+j=a}\operatorname{Tot}(\operatorname{gr}^iP\otimes_R\operatorname{gr}^jQ)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{gr}^a_G T.$$
They are induced by tensoring representatives in filtration steps and then taking their class modulo $G^{a+1}$, and are natural simultaneously for filtration-preserving chain maps in both variables. Consequently they give natural isomorphisms in $D(R)$
$$\operatorname{gr}^a_G T\cong\bigoplus_{i+j=a}\operatorname{gr}^iP\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}\operatorname{gr}^jQ,$$
where the ordinary K-flat derived tensor is that of [lem-pc-derived-tensor-second-factor-functor] with $A=R$; the underlying $T$ represents $P\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}Q$. If $u:P\to P'$ and $v:Q\to Q'$ are filtered quasi-isomorphisms between complexes satisfying these same hypotheses, then $\operatorname{Tot}(u\otimes v)$ is a filtered quasi-isomorphism. Here filtered quasi-isomorphism means quasi-isomorphism on every graded complex. All displayed comparisons are compatible with composition and identities. No spectral sequence, truncation filtration or Tor-of-cohomology formula is asserted.

source.place: Tag 0H7Y, proposition-kunneth-filtered, and its explicit convolution/graded comparison in section-kunneth-spectral-sequence, paragraphs before Tag 0H7W, lemma-kunneth-converges. Finite-filtration specialization, with functoriality and preservation of filtered quasi-isomorphisms expressed at the complex level; cache /home/ubuntu/c1-stacks-review/more-algebra.tex, lines 15425–15520 and 15755–15800.

proof.text: Construct convolution lifts using the image factorization, and construct the filtered tensor map using imageSubobjectMap on the square formed from the coproduct of tensor restriction maps. The subobject inclusions prove the defining lift equations. Lower bounds A,B give the top step at A+B; upper zero bounds C,D give the bottom step at C+D-1 by the coproduct universal property.

Apply the ordinary flat convolution comparison to obtain e_a with its representative equation. Tensor and coproduct closure of categorical flatness and K-flatness give the properties of the underlying tensor and the graded sum. Transport them across e_a. Descend by natural-number induction from an upper zero bound through the step/graded cokernel sequences, using the proved flat-term K-flat extension lemma. This proves all clauses of HasKunnethFiltration.

For simultaneous naturality, precompose both candidate maps with each coprojection and then with the epimorphic tensor of graded projections. The projection squares and monicity of convolution step inclusions identify both composites. Underlying tensor maps prove the identity/composition laws by extensionality of filtered maps.

For a K-flat first factor, the existing source localization counit theorem makes the lax monoidal comparison for Qh invertible; transfer through quotientCompQhIso to the specified Q comparison. Use asIso for c and cgr. Exact countable sums make Q of the graded sum a coproduct. Precompose the diagram by cgr and derive the inverse-e naturality equation by cancelling isomorphisms.

Factor each tensor of graded maps into the right whisker of the first graded map followed by the left whisker of the second. K-flatness makes both quasi-isomorphisms. Stability under discrete colimits gives the coproduct quasi-isomorphism, and the naturality square with e transfers it to the convolution graded map.
